dimensions.assessment: Directly affects federal wildland firefighters, support personnel, and their next-of-kin in cases of critical injury, illness, or line-of-duty death.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of the Interior shall develop a Wildland Fire Management Casualty Assistance Program... to provide assistance to the next-of-kin of--(1) firefighters... and (2) wildland fire support personnel...

dimensions.assessment: Provides substantial and supportive administrative, financial, and counseling services to families during critical medical or death events.
dimensions.evidence: The reimbursement of next-of-kin for expenses associated with travel... centralized, short-term and long-term case management procedures...

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes travel reimbursements and program development, but specific funding levels or appropriations are not stated in the source text.
dimensions.evidence: The reimbursement of next-of-kin for expenses associated with travel to visit a firefighter or wildland fire support personnel...

dimensions.assessment: Directs the Department of the Interior to establish a comprehensive assistance program involving interagency liaison and data collection.
dimensions.evidence: Liaison with the Department of the Interior, the Department of Justice, and the Social Security Administration to ensure prompt and accurate resolution of issues...

dimensions.assessment: Requires program development within 6 months and establishes ongoing case management and support operations.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 6 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall develop a Wildland Fire Management Casualty Assistance Program...

missing_information: Total authorized budget or appropriations for the program and travel reimbursements.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the Secretary of the Interior to develop a casualty assistance program for wildland firefighters and support personnel, providing next-of-kin notifications, travel expense reimbursements, and case management.

card.summary: The Fix Our Forests Act establishes new requirements and programs for managing federal, state, tribal, and private lands to reduce wildfire risks, expedite environmental reviews, and improve forest health. It creates an interagency Fireshed Center to predict and assess fires, establishes emergency management projects in high-risk firesheds, reforms litigation procedures for forest management projects, creates community wildfire risk reduction and research programs, expands utilities' ability to manage vegetation near power lines, and provides casualty assistance for wildland firefighters.
